audit.title: DataLink Architecture (Pull Delivery)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opening — "DataLink (Pull Delivery) provides infrastructure for Data Providers to make their specialized data available onchain…" is a liftable definition. The numbered steps are each self-contained.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: One H1, one section, a clean numbered/bulleted step list (measured: 1 heading, 9 bullets, 0 tables). No H2/H3 subsections and no summary table means an engine can't extract the four architectural stages as discrete retrievable units.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured 4 numerals, 0 with units, no version strings. "Multiple nodes," "low-latency REST and WebSocket," "high availability" are all qualitative — no consensus thresholds, node counts, or latency figures.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 8 internal links, 0 external/primary. Good cross-linking into Data Streams reference/tutorials, but nothing to a spec or canonical primary source.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The lead sentence is quotable; the closing sentence differentiating DataLink from Data Streams ("focuses the DON's role on securely fetching and signing data from a *single provider*") is a strong liftable distinction.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Poor. Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks; acceptable for a conceptual page, but no config/address references either (verifier addresses are only linked, not shown).

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the "what is" concept only. No "how does DataLink differ from Data Streams," no troubleshooting, no lifecycle beyond the flow diagram.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (DataLink, DON, Aggregation Layer, Verifier Contracts), unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a concise, well-written conceptual overview of the DataLink Pull Delivery data-flow, opening with a serviceable canonical definition and linking heavily into the wider Data Streams docs. Its biggest GEO weaknesses are the near-total absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates) and a lack of concrete specifics (no node counts, no latency figures, no version data) — the page describes architecture in qualitative terms only. As a single 265-word section under one H1, it chunks cleanly but offers no symptom- or question-phrased entry points for retrieval, so it will win "what is DataLink architecture" queries but little else.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential `canonical` URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-trust and citation rate for agents that verify source authority.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased subheadings
recommendations.where: convert the four numbered steps and the closing paragraph into H2/H3 sections
recommendations.change: Add H2s like "How does DataLink differ from Data Streams?", "How is the data signed and verified?", "How do dApps fetch DataLink reports?" — each opening with a one-sentence answer.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses; they also create clean per-topic chunks.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete specifics
recommendations.issue: "Multiple nodes… reach consensus"; "low-latency REST and WebSocket APIs."
recommendations.change: State the DON node count / consensus threshold if disclosable, quantify "low-latency" (e.g. p99 latency), and name the report/verifier version or schema. Even "single-provider" report cadence figures help.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for generative visibility; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table (DataLink vs Data Streams)
recommendations.issue: The key distinction is buried in one prose sentence.
recommendations.change: Add a 2-column table contrasting data source (single provider vs aggregated), DON role, and shared transport/verification components.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract *reasons* and build justified comparative answers — a common query shape here.

recommendations.title: Replace the vague quantifier "robust"
recommendations.change: Replace with the concrete property, e.g. "active-active multi-site" transport with the specific HA guarantee.
recommendations.why: Specific properties are liftable; qualifiers are not.

recommendations.title: Add one external/primary citation
recommendations.change: Link the verification claim to the canonical verifier spec or report-format reference.
recommendations.why: Primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier "robust" (flagged in measured facts); "low-latency" and "high availability" used without figures.
"(Image: Image)" — an unlabeled image placeholder with no alt text; provide a descriptive caption so the diagram's content is machine-readable.
No stale-content risk detected, but the *absence* of any date signal is itself a freshness gap.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; confirm this page is indexed there.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD may be injected site-wide at render; the served HTML shows none, so verify at the template level rather than per page.
Diagram alt-text and last-updated cadence are likely controlled by the docs platform, not this page alone.
